text:
Nina (Sales): Heads up - Epoch demo this morning. Customer reports slow TTFT on long seqs and 429s when they ramp from 10->70 rps. Also a 403 when they flip to our VPC private endpoint. They asked for a short Dedicated trial price to prove stability. Can we form a quick triage swarm?
Omar (Solutions): can you drop the exact auth string + any X-Request-ID? also which model variant and seq_len distribution?
Nina (Sales): auth: "perm denied: 403 egress block to model-host-01". request id from their header: r-9f8c2d. Model: rw-chat-medium (pinned), typical seqs 800-1200, 12 concurrent clients doing small chat turns.
Rohit (SRE): 429s on burst = likely per-tenant concurrency or rate window. Ask them to check response headers: X-Redwood-Limit, X-Redwood-Remaining. Also check if they are rotating tokens rapidly (that can trip our anti-abuse).
Leah (Eng Oncall): On the infra side we saw increased host CPU when sequences hit >1024 and increased kv cache thrash. Recent metrics: model.kv_cache.hit_rate ~0.08 over 15m on the shard serving rw-chat-medium. That inflates token generation time.
Marta (Security): For Private/VPC: 403 usually means our egress allowlist doesn't include their NAT IPs or their connector isn't attached to the correct subnet. We also need the completed security questionnaire (especially KMS/HSM answers) before enabling private access.
Nina (Sales): Customer said they used default SDK, batch_window_ms = 10ms, pooling disabled. They're willing to change client settings while we debug.
Omar (Solutions): Quick mitigation steps to ask them to try before the call: 1) set client.batch_window_ms = 30-40ms to allow the SDK to coalesce messages; 2) enable connection pooling and reuse a single session for multiple clients; 3) try a lower concurrency ramp (e.g., 10 -> 30 rps) to measure when 429s start. Also request a small repro payload they can paste.
Ben (Customer Success): I'll schedule a 30m deep-dive with Epoch for 11:00 PST and include SRE + Oncall. Also can offer a 10-day Dedicated demo (single GPU) while we investigate; price TBD but we should be conservative with credits. Legal ok with temporary addendum.
deploy-bot: Deploy v2.14.3 -> prod; note: experimental prefix-cache scheduler rolled back last night.
Leah (Eng Oncall): If cache hit_rate < 0.2 we should enable multi-tenant shared prefix cache for that model and pre-warm with hot prompts. Internal commands to gather traces: ```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN" https://console.redwood.dev/api/traces/r-9f8c2d``` and ```rbxctl metrics query --range 15m "model.kv_cache.hit_rate{model=\"rw-chat-medium\"}"```
Rohit (SRE): Also check tenant-level concurrency allowance: ```rbxctl quota get --tenant epochai``` if they need higher concurrency we can apply a temporary bump for the demo window (ops approval required).
Marta (Security): Nina, get their completed SQ and a list of allowed CIDRs. If they require CMK/HSM we need 2-3 weeks lead time. For quick POC we can use our managed keys if they accept that.
Nina (Sales): I'll collect headers + the SQ doc and ask them to flip batch_window to 35ms before our 11:00 PST call. Thanks team, I'll post results here after the session. :pray:
notes: sales-led POC swarm coordination: VPC 403, burst 429s, KV cache miss rate, client batching changes, Dedicated demo pricing/onboarding
